 WFLA Tampa Follow Flight attendant accused of using travel benefits to steal $20K from Florida woman
 Ashley Suter Tue, October 27, 2026 at 5:02 PM UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Video above: See the week's top headlines in Tampa Bay 
 PALM COAST, Fla. (WFLA)— An American Airlines flight attendant is accused of using her travel benefits and defrauding a 75-year-old Florida woman as part of a sweepstakes scheme.
 Destiny Blake, 24, of Brooklyn, New York, was arrested by U.S. Customs and Border Protection in Miami on Friday after an investigation revealed she took around $23,000 from a 75-year-old Palm Coast woman.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In November 2025, a caller, who claimed to be with Publishers Clearing House, told the victim she had won and to collect her "winnings."
 The victim was then instructed to mail a $500 gift card to "Destiny Blake" at a Brooklyn address, which she did, deputies said.
 During this time, the victim was also locked out of her email address, and the password was changed, and the account had been switched to a look-alike address that she never created.
 Credit: Flagler County Sheriff's Office
 According to deputies, between Nov. 15 and Nov. 19, 2025, the victim withdrew $14,000 from her bank, and Blake received $14,220 in cash and Zelle payments.
 Advertisement Advertisement On Nov. 18, Blake flew from New York to Daytona Beach as a standby passenger using her flight attendant benefits and then took an Uber to a hotel in Palm Coast.
 The next morning, Blake was dropped off at the victim's home just before 11 a.m. and 15 minutes later, an Uber picked her up and took her back to the Daytona Beach airport.
 According to FCSO, before Blake flew home, purchases were made on the victim's credit card at the Daytona Beach airport and Charlotte airport.
 Detectives have determined that Blake was issued her own Apple Card and was an authorized user on the victim's account.
 Deputies said a family member later found a note in the victim's home with instructions to call the card company and tell them Blake was her granddaughter and was authorized to use the card.
 Advertisement Advertisement Between Nov. 16 and Dec. 11, 2025, 88 total charges that totaled to $11,590.30 were charged to the victim's credit card, which included a $1,740.91 eBay order shipped to Blake, a $1,523.16 spent on Apple products and more than $1,300 spent at T-Mobile, Ugg, a hair salon, and dozens of Uber rides and Uber Eats orders.
 FCSO said one of the Uber rides was paid in Jamaican dollars in Kingston, two days after Blake flew there while working for the airline.
 In total, the victim lost around $23,310.
 An arrest warrant was obtained for Blake on Oct. 16, 2026, for the thefts and fraudulent charges.
 "Most flight attendants use their benefits to see the world. Blake used her's to further a scam against a senior resident, live a lavish lifestyle using stolen bank cards and thinking she could get away with it," said Sheriff Rick Staly. "Her wings were clipped by our detectives and with the help of CPB she was arrested. Her next trip? Flagler County to be held accountable for her crimes."
 Advertisement Advertisement Blake was arrested for organized scheme to defraud of $20,000 from a victim 65 or older, fraudulent use of personal identification information of a person 60 or older, and grand theft over $20,000, Flagler County deputies said.
 Blake was taken to the Miami-Dade County Jail, where she was later released on a $30,000 bond.
 The Flagler County Sheriff's Office released the following ways to help elderly victims:
 A step-by-step guide to safeguard loved ones' phones, email, computers, and bank accounts
 Suspected financial exploitation of a vulnerable adult can be reported to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 or the U.S. Department of Justice National Elder Fraud Hotline at 1-833-372-8311
 Advertisement Advertisement FCSO encourages anyone who believes they were targeted in a similar scam or had financial contact with Blake to call the sheriff's office at 386-313-4911.
 WFLA News Channel 8 reached out to American Airlines for a statement.
